Knowing what good looks like, and holding the bar, is the job. For a manager this means coaching engineers in how they plan, direct, review and verify agent work, ensuring there’s a balanced approach and vigilance towards quality, and pushing the team's workflows forward as the tools evolve. Every engineer helps improve how we work instead of only following it. The manager sets that tone: you drive the direction and make room for the team to challenge it. One-on-ones, honest feedback, career growth, and early, fair action when something is not working. Own delivery. Plan with the team, keep commitments visible, remove blockers, and represent the team in planning and product meetings. Partner with product. Work with your product manager daily on priorities and the trade-off between roadmap and technical health. Coach the agentic way of working. Pair with engineers on how they plan, direct and review agent work. Guide, sometimes push, the direction, and bring in what works on other teams. Help the team evolve with our tool-set and best practices. Stay hands-on, off the critical path. Code through agents, review pull requests, and keep your technical judgment current.
